title: Which jump sizes reach both fifteen and thirty?
description: Treasures sit on fifteen and thirty. Every jump size that reaches fifteen also reaches thirty, because thirty is two fifteens, and Keeko's doubt, that only three and five work, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: when one number is a multiple of the other, the jump sizes that reach the smaller reach both. Watch for students who leave out one and the number itself.

source: What jump size can reach both 15 and 30? There are multiple
video_script.why: The child lists the jump sizes that reach fifteen and sees that each also reaches thirty, because thirty is two fifteens.
video_script.substitution: If a number is a multiple of another, the jump sizes that reach the smaller also reach the larger.
video_script.anchor: the treasure game of the book: {{NAME_4}} places treasures on fifteen and thirty and {{NAME_2}} jumps in equal steps
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says only three and five work, because one and fifteen are not real jump sizes. A jump of one reaches every number and a jump of fifteen reaches fifteen and thirty, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The jump sizes are one, three, five and fifteen

final_answer.spoken: the jump sizes are one, three, five and fifteen

names.{{NAME_4}}: places the treasures on numbers in the treasure game
names.{{NAME_2}}: jumps in equal steps from zero in the treasure game

maths_rules: demo: a jump of 3 reaches 12 and carries on to 24, because 24 = 2 x 12
30 = 2 x 15, so every size that reaches 15 reaches 30 too
video_script.design: One idea: the jump sizes that reach fifteen also reach thirty, because thirty is two fifteens. Assumes factors and common factors. Wrong idea: one and fifteen are not real jump sizes. The row stays on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a number row with chests on 15 and 30; {{NAME_4}} and {{NAME_2}} stand at the two ends

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.ask: a question mark appears over the two chests

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the treasure game with two treasures.
<bookmark mark='place'/>{{NAME_4}} places treasures on fifteen and thirty.
<bookmark mark='jump'/>{{NAME_2}} jumps in equal steps from zero.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What jump sizes can reach both treasures? There are many, so we must find them all.

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a chest on 12 and a chest on 24; jumps of 3 land on 12 and carry on to 24

marks.three: jumps of 3 land on 3, 6, 9, 12 and the chest on 12 glows
marks.carry: the jumps go on to 24 and the chest on 24 glows

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Take a jump of three, and a treasure on twelve. It lands on three, six, nine and twelve.
<bookmark mark='carry'/>It carries on and lands on twenty four too, because twenty four is twelve doubled.

marks.given: the two treasures are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, treasures on fifteen and thirty.

beats.on_screen: To find: all the jump sizes that reach both treasures

marks.find: the words To find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find all the jump sizes that reach both.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: sizes that reach 15: 1, 3, 5, 15 (1 x 15, 3 x 5); a size that reaches both must reach 15

marks.must: an arrow shows every jump passing 15 before 30

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step one, list the jump sizes that reach fifteen. They are one, three, five and fifteen.
<bookmark mark='must'/>A jump size that reaches both must reach fifteen first, so no other size can work.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 30 = 2 x 15, so each jump that reaches 15 reaches 30 too: 1 needs 30 jumps, 3 needs 10, 5 needs 6, 15 needs 2

marks.count: the number of jumps is written under each size

narration: <bookmark mark='double'/>Step two, test each size on thirty. Thirty is two times fifteen, so every jump that reaches fifteen reaches thirty as well.
<bookmark mark='count'/>One needs thirty jumps, three needs ten, five needs six, and fifteen needs two.

marks.rest: 5 x 6 = 30 and 15 x 2 = 30 are written and all get a tick

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step three, put each size back. One times thirty is thirty, and three times ten is thirty.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Five times six is thirty, and fifteen times two is thirty.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the jump sizes are 1, 3, 5 and 15
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The jump sizes are one, three, five and fifteen.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble, then struck through; a jump of 1 reaches every number and a jump of 15 reaches 15 and 30

marks.why: 1 and 15 are crossed out in the bubble
marks.one: jumps of 1 cover the row up to 30

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks only three and five work.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Keeko says one and fifteen are not real jump sizes.
<bookmark mark='one'/>But a jump of one reaches every number, thirty included.
<bookmark mark='big'/>A jump of fifteen reaches fifteen and then thirty.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Both are real jump sizes, so the doubt is struck.
